skill.name: scanning-tools
skill.description: Guides authorized security teams through network discovery, vulnerability scanning, web testing, wireless assessment, cloud checks, compliance scanning, and reporting workflows.
skill.summary: Reference guide for authorized security scanning workflows and tool selection.
skill.author: sickn33

security_audit.summary: The static findings are mostly confirmed where the skill provides actionable scanning, privileged execution, wireless attack, and Metasploit workflows. Several parser matches were false positives, including Markdown fence delimiters, localhost UI links, common port references, report conversion, and Nmap syntax mistaken for hard links. The strongest concerns are internet-wide Masscan guidance, wireless deauthentication and cracking steps, and exploit validation with Metasploit.

remediation.suggestion: Remove 0.0.0.0/0 examples and require explicit owned scope, rate limits, and written authorization before any scan workflow.
Remove exploitation and auto-exploit instructions, or replace them with defensive validation concepts that do not launch exploit frameworks.

remediation.issue: Wireless deauthentication and password cracking steps
remediation.suggestion: Remove deauthentication, handshake capture, WPA cracking, and WEP cracking commands from marketplace-facing guidance.
Add explicit confirmation gates and manual-only instructions for sudo, package installation, service startup, and host audit commands.
Use safer credential handling guidance and warn users not to place real API keys in shell history or process arguments.

remediation.issue: Active web scanning and brute-force wording
remediation.suggestion: Frame web testing as authorized-only and remove brute-force language unless strong scope and rate controls are included.

content.value_statement: Security teams need clear scanning plans that match their scope and authorization. This skill maps common tools to network, web, wireless, cloud, compliance, and reporting tasks.
actual_capabilities: Compares tools for network discovery, vulnerability assessment, web testing, wireless review, cloud checks, and compliance scans.
Lists example workflows for Nmap, Masscan, Nessus, OpenVAS, Burp Suite, ZAP, Nikto, Aircrack-ng, Kismet, and Metasploit.
Explains report outputs for network discovery, vulnerability assessment, web application testing, and compliance validation.
Provides a phased methodology from planning through reporting and remediation guidance.
Includes troubleshooting guidance for host discovery, scan speed, and web scanner coverage.
limitations: It does not verify that the user owns or is authorized to scan a target.
Several examples are active scans that can affect networks or trigger monitoring systems.
It does not replace expert validation of vulnerabilities or legal review of scope.
Some tool names, options, and package names may change across platforms.

use_cases.title: Plan an Internal Assessment
use_cases.description: Create a scoped workflow for discovering hosts, identifying services, running vulnerability checks, and reporting risk.

use_cases.title: Choose Web Testing Tools
use_cases.description: Select tools for crawling, passive review, active checks, and manual verification of an authorized web application.

use_cases.title: Prepare Compliance Evidence
use_cases.description: Map compliance scanners and report formats to system audit requirements for controlled environments.

prompt_templates.title: Plan a Basic Scan
prompt_templates.scenario: Beginner planning for an owned environment.
prompt_templates.prompt: Create a low-impact scan plan for my owned subnet. Include scope, tools, rate limits, evidence to collect, and report sections.

prompt_templates.title: Select Tools by Scope
prompt_templates.prompt: Compare scanning tools for my authorized web application and internal network. Recommend when to use each tool and what outputs to review.

prompt_templates.title: Review Findings
prompt_templates.prompt: Help me triage vulnerability scan results. Group likely false positives, high-risk issues, validation steps, and remediation owners.

prompt_templates.title: Design an Audit Workflow
prompt_templates.prompt: Design an authorized security assessment workflow for network, web, cloud, and compliance checks. Include sequencing, safety controls, and reporting deliverables.

output_examples.input: I need to assess an owned internal subnet before a quarterly review.
output: A scoped scan plan with discovery, service detection, vulnerability checks, and reporting phases.
A safety section with authorization, rate limits, maintenance windows, and contact points.
A deliverables list covering host inventory, risk summary, and remediation priorities.

output_examples.input: I have web scanner results and need a report structure.
output: An executive summary format with scope, methodology, key risks, and business impact.
A technical findings section with evidence, validation notes, severity, and remediation guidance.
A false-positive review checklist for authenticated areas and scanner coverage gaps.

output_examples.input: I need to pick cloud and compliance scanning tools.
output: A tool comparison for cloud posture checks, host compliance audits, and report generation.
A recommended sequence that starts with read-only checks and documents required permissions.
A note to validate findings manually before assigning remediation work.

best_practices: Use only on systems where scanning authorization and scope are documented.
Start with passive or low-impact checks before active vulnerability scanning.
Record scan windows, targets, options, findings, and manual validation notes.
anti_patterns: Scanning public targets without written authorization or a defined scope.
Running aggressive scans during business hours without change approval.
Treating scanner output as final proof without manual validation.

faq.question: What does this skill help with?
faq.answer: It helps plan authorized security scans, choose tools, interpret outputs, and structure reports.

faq.question: Can it prove that a target is authorized?
faq.answer: No. Users must provide and verify authorization before any scan is planned or run.

faq.question: Does it run scanners by itself?
faq.answer: No. It provides guidance and example workflows. Tool execution depends on the user environment.

faq.question: Why is this skill high risk?
faq.answer: It includes active scanning, privileged commands, wireless attack steps, and exploitation validation examples.

faq.question: What reports can it help prepare?
faq.answer: It can help outline discovery reports, vulnerability reports, web testing reports, and compliance evidence.

faq.question: Who should use it?
faq.answer: It is intended for trained security staff working inside approved scopes and controlled environments.
